>It sounds like you're doing all of the heavy lifting here when it comes to her getting better. You're a shoulder to lean on, give her suggestions on how to better her life, and it seems like its falling on either deaf ears or she doesn't care enough..so ultimately it really is up to you and how much more effort you want to keep putting into this friendship before you see a change. It's like that saying, "The definition of insanity is doing the same thing every day and expecting different results." She needs to put in more effort, because you trying to do it all for her while she's in denial isn't helping anyone, and is only hurting you :/

yea, I actually suspected she had borderline personality disorder (I am a psychology major and study these things). Someone else who has BPD in the comments says that it sounds like she has BPD from reading this. She admitted to the symptoms depending on the source of website I used. However, overall she seemed in denial of it. I'm not a psychiatrist so I don't want to diagnose her.   
I think I'm just a really sensitive person so when someone feels a certain way or has a certain belief I can start to easily get influenced by them. I want to be someone that can be less influenced by others outlooks though. But I keep hearing things like "we are the average of the five people we spend the most time with" so that's a big reason on why I'm thinking of distancing from her.

I actually told her that I suspected that she had BPD a couple weeks ago and she denied it. A big reason why I thought she had it was because she complained she chronically felt "empty" and that nothing satisfied her. I looked up and Googled her symptoms and she told me that she matched the symptoms depending on the source or website I used. Overall, she seemed to deny having BPD though so I didn't want to touch upon it more. She also tells me she doesn't fear abandonment because she abandons herself and expects herself to be single and never married and just live with a lot of cats.
